source.page_numbering: 1-based physical PDF page; printed page agrees

inspection.geometry_coordinates: points, top-left origin, approximate manual regions; null means multi-page/disjoint evidence
inspection.failed_tool: Bundled pdftoppm could not initialize writable fontconfig cache; interrupted and used already-installed PDFium.

coverage.figure_scope: No standalone illustration, chart, or figure caption found in all-page text and contact-sheet inspection. Vector geometry witnesses are ruled tables and mathematical operators, not figure coverage.
coverage.tables: Two complexity/competitive-factor comparison tables on physical page 13; no empirical numeric data table.
coverage.footnotes: Three footnotes, including cross-page Table 1 note 3.

evaluation_policy.unit: per witness; no aggregate completeness claim
allowed_normalization: Discretionary line-end hyphens removed only to rejoin the original word
Unicode/math equivalent notation preserving all operators, indices, bounds, conditions and labels
evaluation_policy.duplicate_policy: Repeated witnesses earn no additional credit; contradictions, duplicate body text and interleaved noise are failures even when a matching substring exists.
evaluation_policy.image_policy: A complete faithful source crop can pass visual preservation only. An image with no equivalent structured text/math/table content cannot pass accessibility.
required_failure_cases: Long noisy output repeating the source
Missing conditional branches or inequality direction
Wrong row/column, author/year, role or footnote associations
Clipped native crop or invisible mathematical glyph
Silent correction or invention of source mathematics
Raster-only mathematics/table passed as accessible without equivalent content

limits: Oracle is a manually reviewed sample, not an exhaustive proof of semantic completeness.
Full-size visual inspection excludes physical page 2; its raw text and contact-sheet render were inspected.
Source text extraction is evidence for locating prose, not an independent authority for mathematical glyphs; equations were checked against rendered pages.
No reading-device, screen-reader, EPUB/KFX or converter output inspected.
All boxes are coarse locator bounds, not pixel-perfect mask or ownership annotations.
No standalone figure fidelity can be established by this source.

witnesses.source_excerpt: A formal analysis and taxonomy of task allocation in multi-robot systems
acceptance: One title before the abstract.
Brian P. Gerkey belongs to Stanford University; Maja J Matarić belongs to University of Southern California.
Keep the two authors and their affiliations associated, even if author columns reflow.
failures_to_catch: Row-wise mixing of author/affiliation columns.
Title fragments repeated as separate section headings.

witnesses.source_excerpt: Despite more than a decade of experimental work in multi-robot systems, important theoretical aspects of multi-robot coordination mechanisms have, to date, been largely untreated.
acceptance: Abstract is one coherent block ending with “new approaches.”
The heading “1 Introduction” follows the complete abstract in reading order.
The right-column heading “1.1 Multi-Robot Task Allocation (MRTA)” follows the introduction paragraph, not the first abstract lines.
failures_to_catch: Line-wise interleaving of abstract and right column.
Abstract italic text mistaken for a figure.

witnesses.source_excerpt: it is no longer sufficient to show, for example, a pair of robots observing targets or a large group of robots flocking as examples of coordinated robot behavior.
acceptance: Join the bottom-left introduction text “observing targets” to the top-right “or a large group”.
Then finish that paragraph before heading 1.1.
failures_to_catch: Reading the top-right continuation before the abstract.
Inserting author text or page number into the sentence.

witnesses.source_excerpt: Ideally the goal is to directly optimize overall system performance, but that quantity is often difficult to measure during system execution.
acceptance: Heading “3 Utility” begins the bottom-left section.
Join “during sys-” at bottom-left to “tem execution.” at top-right.
Keep the following sentence about alternative task allocations after this join.
failures_to_catch: Starting Utility with the right-column middle paragraph.
Leaving “sys- tem” as separate words.
Treating the page as row-wise prose.

witnesses.source_excerpt: U_RT = { Q_RT − C_RT if R is capable of executing T and Q_RT > C_RT; 0 otherwise }
acceptance: Preserve two branches under one left brace.
The capability condition AND strict Q_RT > C_RT condition belong to the first branch.
Zero is the fallback branch.
RT is a subscript on U, Q and C; minus is subtraction.
failures_to_catch: Losing the brace or second branch.
Changing > to ≥.
Misreading minus as ¡ or hyphenated prose.
Text outside crop or partly clipped condition.
witnesses.representation: Image acceptable for visual fidelity only; accessibility needs equivalent machine-readable cases and condition structure.

acceptance: Keep Q_AT=20, C_AT=10, Q_BT=15, C_BT=5 paired with the correct robots.
The chain establishes equal utility; it is not a numerical table.
failures_to_catch: Dropping a number, subscript or minus.
Inventing preference for robot A from quality alone.

acceptance: One summation with lower limit e∈X.
Equation number (1) remains associated with the sum.
The subset-maximization definition precedes it.
failures_to_catch: Capital X substituted for the summation.
Omitting the lower limit or u(e).
Equation number injected into prose.

witnesses.source_excerpt: Algorithm (The Greedy algorithm).
acceptance: Ordered step 1 sorts u(e1) ≥ u(e2) ≥ … ≥ u(en).
Step 2 sets X := ∅.
Step 3 loops j=1 to n with conditional X ∪ {e_j} ∈ F, then X = X ∪ {e_j}.
Preserve nested conditional structure instead of flattening into an unordered bag of tokens.
failures_to_catch: Treating 1/2/3 as footnote links.
Replacing ∅ with 0.
Dropping the membership guard.

witnesses.source_excerpt: single-task robots (ST) vs. multi-task robots (MT)
acceptance: Three distinct bullets: ST vs MT; SR vs MR; IA vs TA.
ST concerns tasks per robot; SR concerns robots per task; IA concerns assignment horizon.
Keep each explanation under its own bullet.
failures_to_catch: Swapping ST and SR.
Merging bullet labels into the optimal-assignment definition in the other column.

acceptance: Two nested sums with different limits.
Keep α_ij, U_ij and w_j factors in each summand.
Equation (2) is the objective, followed by “subject to”.
failures_to_catch: Dropping weight w_j.
Flattening superscript limits into multiplicative text.
Replacing α with literal ®.

acceptance: Two stacked constraints share label (3).
First sums over i; second sums over j.
Preserve equality to 1 and both ranges exactly as printed.
failures_to_catch: Changing equality to ≤ as a mathematical correction.
Losing either constraint.
Collapsing their index ranges.

acceptance: Definition introduces a dual minimum problem.
Preserve plus between the two sums.
Constraint uses ≥ and universal i,j.
Keep labels (4) and (5) with their own expressions.
failures_to_catch: ≥ becomes > or ≤.
Constraint falsely attached to the opposite-column equation (9).
Equation (4) number becomes start of right-column prose.

witnesses.source_excerpt: t_i = argmax_j {h_ij − p_j}. (6)
acceptance: j is the argmax index.
The braces contain h_ij minus p_j.
The equation belongs after “its profit is maximized”.
failures_to_catch: Missing argmax index.
h and p merged into a word.
Equation rendered as a caption without the defining prose.

witnesses.source_excerpt: u_i = h_it_i − p_t_i, ∀i; v_j = p_j − c_j, ∀j. (7)
acceptance: Equation (7) has two rows, one for robot profit and one for broker profit.
Equation (8) reads h_ij = α_ij and c_j = 0.
Equation (9) reads u_i = α_it_i − p_t_i and v_j = p_j.
Labels (7),(8),(9) must not be read as mathematical factors.
failures_to_catch: Omitting the second row of an aligned equation.
Changing α_ij to U_ij to repair an apparent source inconsistency.
Merging intervening prose into the equations.

witnesses.source_excerpt: The code for our implementation is available from: http://robotics.stanford.edu/~gerkey.
acceptance: Superscript 1 after “Hungarian method” targets this note.
URL has a tilde before gerkey, not » or whitespace.
Note is separate from main flow and does not interrupt the BLE algorithm conclusion.
failures_to_catch: Deleting the URL as furniture.
Treating the footnote as a new paragraph between “and” and its right-column continuation.
Linking marker 1 to the first ordered-list step.

witnesses.source_excerpt: Algorithm (BLE assignment algorithm).
acceptance: Step 1: if any robot remains unassigned, find highest-utility robot-task pair (i,j); otherwise quit.
Step 2 assigns i to j and removes both from consideration.
Step 3 returns to step 1.
The following statement says this is canonical Greedy and OAP is not a matroid.
failures_to_catch: Dropping termination condition.
Preserving labels but scrambling step bodies.
Assigning the right-column analysis as an algorithm step.

witnesses.source_excerpt: n ≤ 11 for robot soccer, which is more than for most current multi-robot systems
acceptance: Join p7 bottom-right “soc-” to p8 top-left “cer,”.
Keep n ≤ 11 and following O(n^3) statement within the same paragraph.
Footnote 1 and page number 7 do not enter the joined sentence.
failures_to_catch: Duplicate soccer fragments.
“soc-” retained as a complete word.
Joining to p8 top-right Greedy paragraph instead.

witnesses.source_excerpt: R || ∑ w_j C_j.
acceptance: Notation is under section 5.2 ST-SR-TA, not the preceding online-assignment subsection.
Preserve double vertical separator and weighted sum.
The adjacent prose says strongly NP-hard, not tractable.
failures_to_catch: Dropping bars as table rules.
Treating the sum as decorative image without equivalent accessible structure.
Losing weighted qualifier.

acceptance: Two vertically stacked large set operators share label (10).
Intersection and union are different glyphs with x∈X below each.
The first equals empty set; the second equals E.
As printed, no explicit operand x appears after either operator; preserve the source rather than silently correcting the mathematics.
failures_to_catch: Both operators turned into slash/backslash.
Empty set becomes zero.
Only one row retained.
Adding mathematical operands not visible in source.

acceptance: Keep large union operator with x∈X beneath it.
As printed, the union has no explicit operand after the operator.
Following prose states that subsets in a cover need not be disjoint.
failures_to_catch: Confusing union with intersection.
Changing need not be disjoint into must be disjoint.
Auto-repairing the source without annotation.

witnesses.source_excerpt: 5.5 MT-SR-IA & MT-SR-TA: Multi-task robots, single-robot tasks
acceptance: One combined subsection heading with both classification triples.
It follows the completion of section 5.4 across columns.
Section 5.6 MT-MR-IA follows this subsection, not an invented 5.5.1.
failures_to_catch: Splitting the ampersand heading into two unrelated sections.

Table-like treatment caused by spaced heading text.

witnesses.source_excerpt: Methodology
acceptance: Section 6 has an ordered three-item list: computation requirements; communication requirements; solution quality.
“Methodology” is a bold run-in label for prose beginning “Computational requirements, or running time”.
Do not manufacture an extra numbered section from the run-in label.
failures_to_catch: List numbers become footnotes or heading levels.
Body prose is all bold because a run-in span leaks style.
Methods text read before section 5.7 conclusion at top-right.

witnesses.source_excerpt: This analysis was originally presented in Gerkey & Matarić (2003)
acceptance: Superscript 2 after “characteristics” points to this note.
Retain the original-publication attribution and separate it from the main paragraph.
failures_to_catch: Deleting note as footer.
Treating marker 2 as list item 2.
Inserting note between “does not” on p11 and “measure” on p12.

witnesses.source_excerpt: In addition to solving the ST-SR-IA problem, the ALLIANCE architecture is also capable of building time-extended task schedules in order to solve a form of the ST-SR-TA problem (see Section 5.2.1).

Do not attach this note to the Table 2 MURDOCH row.
failures_to_catch: Wrong numeric anchor chosen from other source numbers.

witnesses.source_excerpt: Name | Computation / iteration | Communication / iteration | Solution quality
acceptance: Table 1 has four columns, one header row and three architecture rows.
Column divider x coordinates approximately 299,368,449 pt; outer x approximately 95 and 517 pt.
Header row spans approximately y72–96; data rows y96–121,121–145,145–170.
Table 1 caption follows the table and remains separate from Table 2.
failures_to_catch: Column labels detached from cells.
Loss of row/column associations despite all tokens being present.
One image treated as accessible table without an equivalent row/column representation.
witnesses.geometry_note: Approximate manual bounds from a 2x native render, not a segmentation ground-truth tolerance.

witnesses.source_excerpt: ALLIANCE³ (Parker 1998) | O(mn) | O(m) | at least 2-competitive
acceptance: ALLIANCE: computation O(mn), communication O(m), quality “at least 2-competitive”.
BLE (Werger & Matarić 2001): O(mn), O(mn), 2-competitive.
M+ (Botelho & Alami 1999): O(mn), O(mn), 2-competitive.
Preserve “at least” on ALLIANCE only.
failures_to_catch: Swapping computation and communication.
Turning O(m) into O(mn) from nearby rows.
Dropping at least or footnote 3.

witnesses.source_excerpt: Name | Computation / task | Communication / task | Solution quality
acceptance: Table 2 has four columns and three architecture rows beneath its header.
Each computation cell contains two lines: O(1) / bidder and O(m) / auctioneer.
These lines are roles within the same row, not separate architectures.
Table 2 caption describes online assignment and follows the table.
failures_to_catch: Dropping bidder/auctioneer role labels.
Flattening two complexity lines into O(1)/O(m) without role associations.
Merging Table 1 per-iteration header into Table 2 per-task header.

witnesses.source_excerpt: MURDOCH (Gerkey & Matarić 2002b) | O(1) / bidder; O(m) / auctioneer | O(m) | 3-competitive
acceptance: MURDOCH has 3-competitive with no “at least”.
First-price auctions (Dias & Stentz 2001) has “at least 3-competitive”.
Dynamic role assignment (Chaimowicz et al. 2002) has “at least 3-competitive”.
Every row has O(m) communication and the same bidder/auctioneer computation pair.
failures_to_catch: Switching 2-competitive from Table 1 into Table 2.
Applying at least uniformly.
Attaching author/year to adjacent architecture.

witnesses.source_excerpt: These similarities are encouraging because they suggest that, regardless of the details of the robots or tasks in use, the various authors are all studying a common, fundamental problem in autonomous coordination.
acceptance: Join p12 bottom-right “because” to p13 below both tables, left column “they suggest”.
Both floating tables and captions remain separately navigable.
Do not put table text inside this sentence; acceptable semantic placement keeps the sentence contiguous while retaining tables in the nearby source order.
failures_to_catch: Literal page-order stitching that inserts both tables in the middle of the sentence.
Discarding tables to make prose coherent.
Joining “because” to p13 right-column continuation “variety”.
